metaDescription: Corded and battery electric mowers compared by motor amps, deck width and self-propel, so you can choose between a cord and a pack for your lawn.
expertTake: The EGO LM2135SP is the best electric mower here because its self-propel, 21-inch deck and long pack suit the widest range of lawns. The LawnMaster MEB1216K corded model is the value pick for a small, flat yard near an outlet. If your lot is bigger than half an acre, electric walk-behinds of any type are the wrong tool and you should look at a gas or riding machine.
introParagraphs: Electric mowers come in two families that behave very differently: corded machines that never run out of power but drag a cable, and battery machines that roam freely but are limited by their pack. Neither is better in the abstract, and the right one depends on the shape of your yard and where the outlets are.

What they share is simplicity. There is no oil, spark plug, carburetor or stale fuel to manage, the motor starts instantly, and noise is a fraction of a gas engine. The decision comes down to how far you need to reach and how much grass you need to cover.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2135SP 21-inch self-propelled
products.description:
The thing that sets the LM2135SP apart is the Touch Drive handle: you engage self-propel with a palm pressed against a sensor, and the mower moves at the speed your hand dictates. That removes the awkward bail-bar-plus-speed-lever combination on most self-propelled mowers. EGO rates the motor at up to 7.0 ft-lbs of cutting torque, a clear step above the 6.0 ft-lbs of the push LM2112, which matters when the deck is loaded with wet grass.

The tradeoff is price and pack weight. You are paying for a drive system and a larger battery, and the drive draws from the same pack as the blade, so the claimed 60 minutes is for light conditions. On an average half-acre you will typically be glad of the spare pack. Against the push LM2112, which is cheaper and lighter, this is the model for slopes or anyone who dislikes shoving a 21-inch deck.

In year three the wear items are the drive cable and the rear wheel hubs. Pull out clippings from the hub gears after wet cuts, and hose the underdeck gently without wetting the motor. The deck stores upright with the handle folded, which saves space.
products.bestFor: Half-acre lawns with gentle slopes where you want the mower to move itself without a clutter of levers.
pros: Touch-drive handle simplifies self-propel control
Highest torque rating in this lineup
21-inch deck cuts fewer passes
Same pack as the brand's other tools
cons: Self-propel shortens runtime from the claimed 60 minutes
Costs more than the push LM2112

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2112 21-inch push mower
products.description:
For a quarter-acre lawn, the LM2112 gives the same brushless motor and 21-inch deck as the bigger EGO machines but ships with the 56V 4.0Ah pack, good for up to 35 minutes by EGO's own estimate. At 4.0Ah the pack is smaller than the larger 5.0Ah or 7.5Ah options in EGO's range, which is the main reason runtime is shorter than the LM2135SP.

The real decision here is whether to buy this and a spare, or step up. If you mow flat grass weekly, the 35-minute figure is enough for about a quarter acre, and the lighter push design avoids the weight and complexity of self-propel. On hills, you will notice the lack of drive immediately, and the LM2135SP becomes the better value.

Treat the battery as the main consumable. Keep it indoors, store it partly charged for winter, and replace the blade yearly. Since the pack also powers EGO's trimmers and blowers, a single battery family can cover the whole yard.
products.bestFor: Flat quarter-acre lawns where you want EGO's motor without paying for self-propel.
pros: Brushless motor shares platform with other EGO tools
21-inch deck on a lighter push body
Quiet and instant start
Battery is compatible across the brand's range
cons: 4.0Ah pack limits runtime to about 35 minutes

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-inch push mower
products.description:
Greenworks builds this around a molded poly deck that the company says is 35% lighter than a steel deck, and the whole machine follows that philosophy: it is a small, easy-handling mower for lots up to about a third of an acre. The push-button start removes the pull cord and keeps the dust out of the user's shoulder.

Compared with the 21-inch EGO machines you take many more passes, but you gain simplicity and a lighter machine to lift into a shed or carry up steps. It is a good match for those who find a full-size mower unwieldy. Against the corded options here, it frees you from managing an extension lead around garden beds.

Poly decks need less paint attention than steel but can crack on a hard strike, so keep the lawn clear of stones. After each cut, tip the machine on its side only if the manual allows, or hose from below. The 40V pack is shared with Greenworks' 40V tool family. Because the pack is a 40V 4.0Ah unit, the energy budget is far below what the EGO 56V machines carry, so treat the third-of-an-acre claim as a ceiling for dry, even grass. If you mow every five days instead of every ten, the grass is shorter and the pack lasts noticeably longer, which is the cheapest runtime upgrade there is.
products.bestFor: Small lawns where weight and storage space matter more than cutting width.
pros: Poly deck keeps total weight low
Push-button start with no pull cord
Five height positions for routine mowing
No cord to snag on beds
cons: Limited to roughly a third of an acre per charge

products.name: LawnMaster MEB1216K 16-inch corded mower
products.description:
A corded mower never loses power partway through a lawn, and the MEB1216K leans into that with a 12-amp motor turning the blade at around 3,500 rpm. A 12-amp draw is close to the limit of a standard 15-amp household circuit with a long extension, so use a heavy-gauge outdoor cord rated for the load, not a thin one that will heat up.

The 16-inch deck and five height positions starting at 1.4 inches suit a small, flat, regularly cut yard. Against the 15-inch BILT HARD corded model, this one is a little wider and has a slightly stronger motor on paper, and against the battery picks it saves the cost of a pack and charger entirely.

The ownership catch is the cord itself. Plan your mowing pattern so the cord stays behind you, and inspect it for nicks before each season. A bypass loop or cord clip on the handle keeps it from pulling out of the outlet. With no battery to degrade, the machine itself ages gracefully.
products.bestFor: Small flat lawns within cord reach of an outlet where you want to skip batteries entirely.
pros: No battery to degrade or recharge
12 amp motor cuts continuously
Lower overall cost than a battery kit
Simple, reliable motor design
cons: Cord limits reach and needs careful handling
16-inch deck is narrow for large lawns

products.name: BILT HARD 15-inch corded mower with bag
products.description:
This is the lightest corded option on the list at about 21 pounds, and it folds down for storage, which is the main reason to choose it. The 11-amp motor spins the blade at about 3,300 rpm, a touch below the LawnMaster, but on a small suburban strip of grass the difference is hard to feel.

The 35-liter bag is the smallest on the list, so expect more stops to empty it than with a bigger collector. For a pocket-sized lawn that is fine, but if you have a quarter acre it becomes a chore, and the battery EGO or Greenworks machines are a better fit.

Ownership comes down to cord care and keeping the deck clean. Wipe the underdeck after each cut, and store it folded in a corner. It is a no-fuss machine, though thin build means it won't take abuse from rocks or roots. One practical habit pays off with every corded mower: start the cut at the outlet and work away in strips so the cable always trails over mown grass, never over the patch you are about to cut. Loop the cord through a strain relief on the handle so a tug cannot pull the plug out mid-pass. Against the LawnMaster, the BILT HARD gives up a little deck width and motor strength to gain a lighter, foldable body, which is the right trade only if carrying and storage are your main headache.
products.bestFor: Townhouse lawns and apartment-block grass strips where storage space is tight.
pros: Light at about 21 pounds for easy handling
Folds for compact storage
11 amp motor is plenty for small turf
Five height positions
cons: Lighter build is less forgiving on rough ground

buyingCriteria.explanation: A corded mower such as the LawnMaster MEB1216K never runs out of charge but is tied to an outlet and a cable you must keep behind you. A battery mower like the EGO LM2112 gives freedom but is capped by its pack. Choose corded if your whole yard sits within cord range, and battery if it does not.

On corded machines the amp rating is the useful number: the MEB1216K is 12 amps and the BILT HARD is 11. On battery mowers the torque rating is more meaningful, such as the EGO's 6.0 and 7.0 ft-lbs. Do not compare amps with ft-lbs, because they describe different machines.

A 15 or 16-inch deck suits lawns of a few thousand square feet, while a 21-inch deck is better for a quarter to half acre. The EGO machines are 21 inches, while the Greenworks 40V is 16 and the BILT HARD is 15. Narrower decks need more passes and more time.

Self-propel is worth it on slopes or with a full bag. The EGO LM2135SP is the only self-propelled machine here, and it draws from the same pack as the blade, so runtime falls compared with a push model. On flat lawns, a push mower is lighter and cheaper.

A 12-amp corded mower needs an outdoor-rated cord of adequate gauge, typically 14 gauge or heavier for longer runs. A thin cord overheats and drops voltage, which lowers blade speed. This is the most common mistake corded buyers make.

The BILT HARD folds and weighs around 21 pounds, the Greenworks 40V uses a lighter poly deck, and the EGO machines store upright. If you carry the mower up steps or keep it in a cramped shed, weight and fold design matter as much as cutting power.

specDecoder.meaning: The current the motor draws at full load. More amps generally means more cutting power, up to the circuit's limit.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LawnMaster MEB1216K is 12 amp, the BILT HARD is 11 amp.

specDecoder.meaning: A measure of how hard the motor pushes against grass resistance. More torque means less stalling in thick turf.
specDecoder.watchFor: EGO rates the LM2112 at up to 6.0 and the LM2135SP at up to 7.0.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade rotation speed. Higher rpm gives a cleaner cut and better lift, but only if the motor can hold that speed under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MEB1216K lists 3,500 rpm, the BILT HARD 3,300.

specDecoder.meaning: Minutes of mowing on a full battery in light conditions. Thick or wet grass reduces this.
specDecoder.watchFor: EGO claims up to 35 minutes on the LM2112 and up to 60 on the LM2135SP.

specDecoder.meaning: Steel is rigid, while poly is lighter and rust-proof. Each has tradeoffs in weight and impact resistance.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks 40V poly deck is 35% lighter than steel by the maker's claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated corded and battery machines because the buying logic differs. We looked at amps for the cords and torque for the batteries. The result is a lineup of two corded and three battery mowers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Deck and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared deck widths from 15 to 21 inches and the weight of each machine. The 21-inch EGO decks cover ground fastest, while the 15-inch BILT HARD is easiest to carry. We noted deck material and fold design too.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drive and torque
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the one self-propelled machine and the torque ratings of the EGO pair. We weighted drive and torque higher for larger and sloped lawns, and lower for small flat ones.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed upkeep from the spec sheets: batteries, cords, decks, and storage. We prefer designs that are simple to clean and store. The judgments are based on owner feedback patterns and published specifications.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lot-size match
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each machine to the lawn size its maker claims it handles, such as the Greenworks 40V's third of an acre. We marked down machines when buyers would likely stretch them past that range.

rows: Small flat yard near a socket

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The LawnMaster MEB1216K and BILT HARD never run flat, cost less, and avoid battery wear. The price is a cable you have to manage and a reach limited by cord length. Ideal for small yards close to an outlet.

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: The EGO LM2112, EGO LM2135SP and Greenworks 40V go anywhere on the property. The tradeoff is a runtime cap and eventual pack replacement. Best for larger or oddly shaped lawns with no outlet nearby.

howToChoose.note: Pick corded for tiny, near-outlet lawns, and battery for anything where a cord would snag.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Light weight, a folding handle and a deck narrow enough to turn around beds. Also check that you can reach the whole lawn within cord range if you pick a corded model.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BILT HARD 15-inch folds and weighs about 21 pounds, while the Greenworks 40V poly deck keeps weight low and adds battery freedom. Both fit a small lawn without feeling oversized.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your lawn has slopes or exceeds a quarter acre. The EGO LM2135SP adds self-propel and torque for that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your yard is small, flat and near an outlet. The LawnMaster MEB1216K does the job with no battery cost.

maintenance.why: Nicks and exposed copper are a shock and fire risk. Replace the extension lead rather than taping it.
A dull blade strains the motor and tears the lawn. A balanced blade also reduces vibration.
Packed clippings choke airflow and promote rust on steel decks. Rinse gently and keep water off the motor.
Heat and cold shorten pack life. Store at partial charge, not empty or full.
Self-propel and wheel gears jam with mud and grass. Clear them to keep drive smooth.

faq.q: Is a corded mower better than a battery mower?
faq.a: Neither is better in general. Corded machines never run out of power but need a cord and an outlet, while battery machines roam free but are limited to their pack's runtime.

faq.q: What extension cord does a corded mower need?
faq.a: A 12-amp mower needs an outdoor-rated cord of heavy gauge, usually 14 gauge or thicker for longer runs. Thin cords overheat and drop voltage, which weakens the cut.

faq.q: Are electric mowers cheaper to run than gas?
faq.a: Yes, since there is no fuel, oil or spark plug to buy. The main running cost is eventual battery replacement for cordless models, while corded machines have almost none.

faq.q: Does higher amperage always mean more power?
faq.a: Amps describe current draw, and a higher figure generally means a stronger motor on the same type of machine. It is only comparable between corded mowers, such as the 12-amp LawnMaster and the 11-amp BILT HARD.

faq.q: Can an electric mower cut wet grass?
faq.a: It can, but wet grass clumps, clogs the deck and cuts runtime on battery models. Waiting for the lawn to dry gives a better result and less strain on the motor.

faq.q: How long does an electric mower last?
faq.a: The machine usually outlasts its batteries. Corded models have simpler motors with less to fail, while cordless packs gradually lose capacity after several seasons.
